questions.prompt: In a right triangle, define \(\sin\theta\) using side lengths.
questions.answer:
For an acute angle \(\theta\) in a right triangle,
\[\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}.\]
The opposite side is across from \(\theta\), and the hypotenuse is the longest side.

questions.prompt: On the unit circle, what are the coordinates of the point corresponding to angle \(\theta\)?
questions.answer:
The unit-circle point is
\[(\cos\theta,\sin\theta).\]
The horizontal coordinate is cosine, and the vertical coordinate is sine.

questions.prompt: Find \(\tan\theta\) if the opposite side is \(6\) and the adjacent side is \(8\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}.\]
So
\[\tan\theta=\frac68=\frac34.\]

questions.prompt: State the period of \(\sin x\) and \(\tan x\).
questions.answer:
Sine repeats every \(2\pi\):
\[\sin(x+2\pi)=\sin x.\]
Tangent repeats every \(\pi\):
\[\tan(x+\pi)=\tan x.\]

questions.prompt: If \(\sin\theta=\frac{5}{13}\) and \(\cos\theta=\frac{12}{13}\), find \(\tan\theta\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}.\]
Then
\[\tan\theta=\frac{5/13}{12/13}=\frac5{12}.\]

questions.prompt: Find \(\sec\theta\) when \(\cos\theta=-\frac14\).
questions.answer:
Secant is the reciprocal of cosine:
\[\sec\theta=\frac1{\cos\theta}.\]
Thus
\[\sec\theta=\frac1{-1/4}=-4.\]

questions.prompt: A point on the unit circle is \(\left(-\frac35,\frac45\right)\). Find \(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\), and \(\tan\theta\).
questions.answer:
On the unit circle, \((x,y)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\).
So
\[\cos\theta=-\frac35,\qquad \sin\theta=\frac45.\]
Then
\[\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{4/5}{-3/5}=-\frac43.\]

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{2}\right)\) using periodicity.
questions.answer:
Sine has period \(2\pi\). Since
\[\frac{5\pi}{2}=2\pi+\frac\pi2,\]
we have
\[\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{2}\right)=\sin\left(\frac\pi2\right)=1.\]

questions.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse \(10\) and side adjacent to \(\theta\) equal to \(6\). Find \(\cos\theta\) and \(\sec\theta\).
questions.answer:
By definition,
\[\cos\theta=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac6{10}=\frac35.\]
Secant is reciprocal cosine, so
\[\sec\theta=\frac1{3/5}=\frac53.\]

questions.prompt: For \(\theta=\pi\), find \(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\), and \(\tan\theta\).
questions.answer:
At angle \(\pi\), the unit-circle point is \((-1,0)\).
Therefore
\[\cos\pi=-1,\qquad \sin\pi=0.\]
Then
\[\tan\pi=\frac{\sin\pi}{\cos\pi}=\frac0{-1}=0.\]

questions.prompt: Explain why \(\tan\left(\frac\pi2\right)\) is undefined.
questions.answer:
Tangent is
\[\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}.\]
At \(\theta=\frac\pi2\),
\[\sin\frac\pi2=1,\qquad \cos\frac\pi2=0.\]
So
\[\tan\frac\pi2=\frac10,\]
which is undefined because division by zero is not allowed.

questions.prompt: A force of magnitude \(20\) N makes angle \(\theta\) with the positive \(x\)-axis. Write its horizontal and vertical components using trig functions, and evaluate them if \(\cos\theta=0.6\) and \(\sin\theta=0.8\).
questions.answer:
For magnitude \(20\), the components are
\[F_x=20\cos\theta,\qquad F_y=20\sin\theta.\]
Substitute the given values:
\[F_x=20(0.6)=12\text{ N},\qquad F_y=20(0.8)=16\text{ N}.\]

questions.prompt: Find all \(x\) in \([0,2\pi)\) for which \(\sin x=0\).
questions.answer:
On the unit circle, \(\sin x\) is the vertical coordinate. It is zero on the horizontal axis.
In \([0,2\pi)\), this occurs at
\[x=0\quad\text{and}\quad x=\pi.\]
The value \(2\pi\) is not included in the interval.

questions.prompt: Find all \(x\) in \([0,2\pi)\) for which \(\cos x=0\).
questions.answer:
On the unit circle, \(\cos x\) is the horizontal coordinate. It is zero on the vertical axis.
In \([0,2\pi)\), this happens at
\[x=\frac\pi2\quad\text{and}\quad x=\frac{3\pi}{2}.\]

questions.prompt: For which real \(x\) is \(\sec x\) undefined?
questions.answer:
Secant is
\[\sec x=\frac1{\cos x}.\]
It is undefined when \(\cos x=0\). This occurs at
\[x=\frac\pi2+k\pi,\quad k\in\mathbb Z.\]
So \(\sec x\) is undefined at all odd multiples of \(\frac\pi2\).

questions.prompt: For which real \(x\) is \(\cot x\) undefined?
questions.answer:
Cotangent is
\[\cot x=\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}.\]
It is undefined when \(\sin x=0\). This occurs at
\[x=k\pi,\quad k\in\mathbb Z.\]
Those are exactly the angles on the horizontal axis of the unit circle.

questions.prompt: A student claims \(\sin(x+\pi)=\sin x\) because sine is periodic. Correct the claim.
questions.answer:
Sine's period is \(2\pi\), not \(\pi\). In fact, adding \(\pi\) moves to the opposite point on the unit circle, so the vertical coordinate changes sign:
\[\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x.\]
The correct periodic statement is
\[\sin(x+2\pi)=\sin x.\]

questions.prompt: Show from the unit circle that \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\).
questions.answer:
The unit-circle point at angle \(\theta\) is
\[(\cos\theta,\sin\theta).\]
Every point on the unit circle has distance \(1\) from the origin, so its coordinates satisfy
\[x^2+y^2=1.\]
Substitute \(x=\cos\theta\) and \(y=\sin\theta\):
\[\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1.\]

questions.prompt: Explain why tangent has period \(\pi\) even though sine and cosine each have period \(2\pi\).
questions.answer:
Tangent is
\[\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}.\]
Adding \(\pi\) changes both sine and cosine signs:
\[\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x,\qquad \cos(x+\pi)=-\cos x.\]
Therefore
\[\tan(x+\pi)=\frac{-\sin x}{-\cos x}=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\tan x,\]
where tangent is defined.

questions.prompt: A moving point on a unit circle has position \((\cos t,\sin t)\), where \(t\) is in radians. Explain why each coordinate is bounded between \(-1\) and \(1\), and identify when the horizontal coordinate is \(1\).
questions.answer:
The point lies on the unit circle, whose radius is \(1\). No horizontal or vertical coordinate can have magnitude greater than the radius, so
\[-1\le\cos t\le1,\qquad -1\le\sin t\le1.\]
The horizontal coordinate is \(1\) at the rightmost point of the circle. That occurs when
\[t=2k\pi,\quad k\in\mathbb Z.\]
